subject: maths
title: Mental Strategies and Number Sentences
seo_title: Year 3 Mental Strategies and Number Sentences Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Extend and apply knowledge of addition and subtraction facts to 20 to develop efficient mental strategies for computation with larger numbers without a calculator
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on mental strategies and number sentences: use facts to 20 with bigger numbers, bridge to 10, near doubles, compensation, fact families and finding the unknown. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the Australian Curriculum and useful for NAPLAN.
key_big: Use the facts to 20 you know to work out bigger sums in your head.
key_sub: 7 + 8 = 15, so 70 + 80 = 150 and 47 + 8 = 55. Round and fix: 39 + 26 = 40 + 26 − 1 = 65. Use the inverse to find the unknown: ? + 45 = 120, so ? = 120 − 45 = 75.
body_html:
Use the facts you know

If you know the facts to 20, you know much more. 7 + 8 = 15, so 7 tens + 8 tens = 15 tens. That means 70 + 80 = 150. The ones digits tell you 47 + 8 = 55, because 7 + 8 = 15.

FactTensHundredsOnes
7 + 8 = 1570 + 80 = 150700 + 800 = 150047 + 8 = 55
13 − 5 = 8130 − 50 = 801300 − 500 = 80063 − 5 = 58

Four mental strategies

Bridge to 10. Jump to the next ten first, then add the rest.

Jump strategy. Keep the first number. Jump the tens, then the ones.

Near doubles. 25 + 26 is double 25 and 1 more: 50 + 1 = 51.

Compensation. Round one number to a ten, then fix it.

Example

What is 39 + 26?

39 is 1 less than 40. 40 + 26 = 66. You added 1 too many, so take it away: 66 − 1 = 65.

Answer: 65

Example

What is 72 − 29?

29 is 1 less than 30. 72 − 30 = 42. You took away 1 too many, so add it back: 42 + 1 = 43.

Answer: 43

Addition and subtraction undo each other

Addition and subtraction are inverse operations. Three numbers make a fact family.

Find the unknown in a number sentence

The = sign means both sides have the same value. Use the inverse to find the missing number.

Example

? + 45 = 120

Use the inverse: 120 − 45 = 75. Check: 75 + 45 = 120.

Answer: 75

Example

300 − ? = 175

Count on from 175: 175 + 25 = 200, then 200 + 100 = 300. 25 + 100 = 125.

Answer: 125

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Compensating the wrong way: 39 + 26 = 67You added 1 too many, so take 1 away: 65
Forgetting to compensate: 39 + 26 = 66Always fix the number you rounded: 66 − 1 = 65
Losing the zero: 70 + 80 = 15 (or 1500)7 tens + 8 tens = 15 tens = 150
Giving the total as the unknown: ? + 45 = 120, ? = 120120 is the whole. Find the part: 120 − 45 = 75
Taking the smaller digit from the larger: 72 − 29 = 57Bridge or compensate: 72 − 30 + 1 = 43

faq.q: What mental strategies do Year 3 students learn?
faq.a: Year 3 students use facts to 20 to work with bigger numbers, and learn to bridge to 10, jump along an empty number line, use near doubles and use compensation, such as 39 + 26 = 40 + 26 − 1 = 65.

faq.q: What is the compensation strategy in maths?
faq.a: You change one number to a friendly ten, work it out, then fix the answer. For 72 − 29, take away 30 to get 42, then add back the extra 1 to get 43.

faq.q: How do you find the missing number in a number sentence?
faq.a: Use the inverse operation. For ? + 45 = 120, work out 120 − 45 = 75, then check that 75 + 45 = 120.

faq.q: Is mental maths important for NAPLAN in Year 3?
faq.a: Yes. The Year 3 NAPLAN numeracy test is done without a calculator, so quick mental strategies and number sentences help students work accurately.

sets.title: Use facts to 20 with bigger numbers

items.q: 7 + 8 = 15. Use this fact. What is 70 + 80?
items.e: 70 is 7 tens and 80 is 8 tens. 7 tens + 8 tens = 15 tens = 150.

items.q: 9 + 5 = 14. Use this fact. What is 90 + 50?
items.e: 90 is 9 tens and 50 is 5 tens. 9 tens + 5 tens = 14 tens = 140.

items.q: 4 + 9 = 13. Use this fact. What is 40 + 90?
items.e: 40 is 4 tens and 90 is 9 tens. 4 tens + 9 tens = 13 tens = 130.

items.q: 15 − 7 = 8. Use this fact. What is 150 − 70?
items.e: 150 is 15 tens and 70 is 7 tens. 15 tens − 7 tens = 8 tens = 80.

items.q: 12 − 5 = 7. Use this fact. What is 120 − 50?
items.e: 120 is 12 tens and 50 is 5 tens. 12 tens − 5 tens = 7 tens = 70.

items.q: 13 − 4 = 9. Use this fact. What is 130 − 40?
items.e: 130 is 13 tens and 40 is 4 tens. 13 tens − 4 tens = 9 tens = 90.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 80 + 60?
items.e: 80 is 8 tens and 60 is 6 tens. Use 8 + 6 = 14: 14 tens = 140.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 140 − 90?
items.e: 140 is 14 tens and 90 is 9 tens. Use 14 − 9 = 5: 5 tens = 50.

items.q: 7 + 8 = 15. Use this fact. What is 47 + 8?
items.e: 7 + 8 = 15, which is 1 ten and 5 ones. So the tens go up by 1: 47 + 8 = 55.

items.q: What is 36 + 9?
items.e: 6 + 9 = 15, which is 1 ten and 5 ones. So the tens go up by 1: 36 + 9 = 45.

items.q: 8 + 5 = 13. Use this fact. What is 68 + 5?
items.e: 8 + 5 = 13, which is 1 ten and 3 ones. So the tens go up by 1: 68 + 5 = 73.

items.q: What is 256 + 7?
items.e: 6 + 7 = 13, which is 1 ten and 3 ones. So the tens go up by 1: 256 + 7 = 263.

items.q: What is 485 + 9?
items.e: 5 + 9 = 14, which is 1 ten and 4 ones. So the tens go up by 1: 485 + 9 = 494.

items.q: 13 − 5 = 8. Use this fact. What is 63 − 5?
items.e: You cannot take 5 from 3 ones. Use 13 − 5 = 8. The tens go down by 1: 63 − 5 = 58.

items.q: What is 42 − 7?
items.e: You cannot take 7 from 2 ones. Use 12 − 7 = 5. The tens go down by 1: 42 − 7 = 35.

items.q: 11 − 6 = 5. Use this fact. What is 81 − 6?
items.e: You cannot take 6 from 1 one. Use 11 − 6 = 5. The tens go down by 1: 81 − 6 = 75.

items.q: What is 234 − 8?
items.e: You cannot take 8 from 4 ones. Use 14 − 8 = 6. The tens go down by 1: 234 − 8 = 226.

items.q: What is 352 − 6?
items.e: You cannot take 6 from 2 ones. Use 12 − 6 = 6. The tens go down by 1: 352 − 6 = 346.

items.q: 6 + 7 = 13. Use this fact. What is 600 + 700?
items.e: 6 hundreds + 7 hundreds = 13 hundreds = 1300.

items.q: 15 − 8 = 7. Use this fact. What is 1500 − 800?
items.e: 1500 is 15 hundreds. 15 hundreds − 8 hundreds = 7 hundreds = 700.

sets.title: Mental strategies: bridge, jump, double, compensate

items.q: Jump to 60 first. What is 58 + 7?
Jump to 90 first. What is 86 + 6?
Jump back to 50 first. What is 53 − 8?
To work out 38 + 7, you jump to 40 first. How do you split the 7?
items.e: 38 needs 2 to make 40. Then 5 more: 40 + 5 = 45. So split 7 into 2 and 5.

items.q: To work out 64 − 9, you jump back to 60 first. How do you split the 9?
items.e: 64 − 4 = 60. Then 5 more: 60 − 5 = 55. So split 9 into 4 and 5.

items.q: Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 45 + 32?
items.e: 45 + 30 = 75. Then 75 + 2 = 77. (75 stops after the tens.)

items.q: Jump back the tens, then the ones. What is 86 − 43?
items.e: 86 − 40 = 46. Then 46 − 3 = 43. (46 stops after the tens.)

items.q: Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 158 + 25?
Jump back the tens, then the ones. What is 124 − 36?
Use double 25. What is 25 + 26?
items.e: Double 25 is 50. 26 is 1 more than 25, so add 1: 50 + 1 = 51.

items.q: Use a near double. What is 35 + 36?
items.e: Double 35 is 70. 36 is 1 more, so 70 + 1 = 71. (61 forgets the ten from 5 + 6 = 11.)

items.q: Use double 40. What is 40 + 39?
items.e: Double 40 is 80. 39 is 1 less than 40, so take away 1: 80 − 1 = 79.

items.q: Use a near double. What is 150 + 160?
items.e: Double 150 is 300. 160 is 10 more than 150, so add 10: 300 + 10 = 310.

items.q: Which double helps with 45 + 46?
items.e: 46 is 1 more than 45. So double 45 is 90, then add 1: 91. The answer is 45 + 45, then add 1.

items.q: Add 40, then take away 1. What is 39 + 26?
items.e: 39 is 1 less than 40. 40 + 26 = 66. You added 1 too many, so take it away: 66 − 1 = 65.

items.q: Use compensation. What is 54 + 29?
items.e: 29 is 1 less than 30. 54 + 30 = 84. You added 1 too many, so take it away: 84 − 1 = 83.

items.q: Use compensation. What is 67 + 19?
items.e: 19 is 1 less than 20. 67 + 20 = 87. You added 1 too many, so take it away: 87 − 1 = 86.

items.q: Use compensation. What is 72 − 29?
items.e: 29 is 1 less than 30. 72 − 30 = 42. You took away 1 too many, so add it back: 42 + 1 = 43.

items.q: Use compensation. What is 145 − 98?
items.e: 98 is 2 less than 100. 145 − 100 = 45. You took away 2 too many, so add them back: 45 + 2 = 47.

items.q: Which shows a good way to work out 39 + 26?
items.e: 39 is 1 less than 40. Add 40, then take away the extra 1: 40 + 26 − 1 = 65.

items.q: Which addition matches the model?
items.e: Add the two parts to make the whole: 36 + 47 = 83.

items.q: Which subtraction matches the model?
items.e: Start with the whole and take away one part. The other part is left: 150 − 90 = 60.

items.q: Addition and subtraction are inverse operations. What does this mean?
items.e: Inverse means opposite. If you add 30 and then take away 30, you are back where you started. They undo each other.

items.q: How many facts are in the fact family for 30, 50 and 80?
28 + 55 = 83. Which is also true?
items.e: Subtraction undoes addition. Start with the whole, 83, and take away 55: 83 − 55 = 28.

items.q: 120 − 70 = 50. Which is also true?
items.e: Addition undoes subtraction. Add the two parts to get back to 120: 50 + 70 = 120.

items.q: Start with 64. Add 29. Then take away 29. What number do you get?
items.e: Taking away 29 undoes adding 29. You get back to the start: 64.

items.q: You know 46 + 37 = 83. What is 83 − 46?
items.e: 46 and 37 are the parts and 83 is the whole. Whole − one part = the other part: 37.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: Whole − part = the other part. 120 − 45: 120 − 40 = 80, then 80 − 5 = 75. Check: 45 + 75 = 120.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: Count on from 130 to 200: 130 + 70 = 200. The missing part is 70.

items.q: What is the whole?
items.e: The whole is the two parts added. 38 + 47: 38 + 40 = 78, then 78 + 7 = 85.

items.q: Which is NOT in the fact family for 25, 40 and 65?
items.e: 40 − 25 is 15, not 65. The whole, 65, must come first in a subtraction. So 40 − 25 = 65 is not in the family.

items.q: Which is NOT in the fact family for 60, 90 and 150?
items.e: It is true, but it uses 30, and 30 is not one of the three numbers. So 90 − 60 = 30 is not in the family.

items.q: Which addition checks that 92 − 58 = 34 is right?
items.e: Add the answer and the number you took away. You should get back to 92: 34 + 58 = 92.

items.q: Which subtraction checks that 67 + 25 = 92 is right?
items.e: Take away the number you added. You should get back to 67: 92 − 25 = 67.
250 and 180 are the parts and 430 is the whole. 430 − 180 = 250. No need to work it out again.

items.q: What is the missing part?
What is the whole?
Mia works out 81 − 27 = 64. To check, she adds 64 + 27 and gets 91, not 81. What is 81 − 27?
items.e: The check shows 64 is wrong. 81 − 27: 81 − 20 = 61, then 61 − 7 = 54. Check: 54 + 27 = 81.

items.q: Noah says 145 + 38 = 173. Use subtraction to check. Is he right?

sets.title: Find the unknown in a number sentence

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 45 = 120
items.e: Use the inverse: 120 − 45. 120 − 40 = 80, then 80 − 5 = 75. Check: 75 + 45 = 120. (120 is the total, not the missing part.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 57 + ? = 100
Find the missing number: 68 = ? + 30
items.e: The = sign means both sides are the same. ? + 30 = 68, so 68 − 30 = 38. Check: 38 + 30 = 68.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 26 = 81
Find the missing number: 90 − ? = 35
Find the missing number: ? − 40 = 85
items.e: Use the inverse: 85 + 40 = 125. Check: 125 − 40 = 85. (45 takes away instead of adding.)

items.q: Find the missing number: ? − 25 = 48
Find the missing number: 140 = 90 + ?
Find the missing number: 200 − ? = 120
items.e: Count on from 120 to 200: 8 tens = 80. Check: 200 − 80 = 120.

items.q: Find the missing number: 300 − ? = 175
Find the missing number: 500 − ? = 350
Find the missing number: ? + 175 = 300
items.e: Use the inverse: 300 − 175. Count on 25 to 200 and 100 to 300: 125. Check: 125 + 175 = 300.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? − 130 = 270
Find the missing number: 650 = ? + 280
Find the missing number: 40 + 25 = ? + 30
items.e: Both sides must have the same value. 40 + 25 = 65, so ? + 30 = 65 and ? = 35. (65 is only the left side.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 70 + 50 = 60 + ?
Find the missing number: 100 − 30 = ? − 40
Find the missing number: 38 + 9 = ? + 10
items.e: 10 is 1 more than 9, so the other number must be 1 less than 38: 37. Check: 38 + 9 = 47 and 37 + 10 = 47.

items.q: Find the missing number: 64 − 19 = ? − 20
Which number sentence is true?
items.e: 45 + 15 = 60 and 70 − 10 = 60. Both sides are the same, so 45 + 15 = 70 − 10 is true.

sets.title: Word problems: choose the number sentence

items.q: Harper has 45 stickers. She gets some more. Now she has 120 stickers. Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: Start with 45, add an unknown amount, and end with 120: 45 + ? = 120. The missing number is 75.

items.q: The canteen had 300 icy poles. Some were sold. Now 175 are left. Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: Start with 300, take away an unknown amount, and 175 are left: 300 − ? = 175. The missing number is 125.

items.q: Some students are on a bus. 30 more get on. Now there are 68 students on the bus. Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: We do not know the start. Add 30 to get 68: ? + 30 = 68. The missing number is 38.

items.q: Ava reads 47 pages on Monday and 38 pages on Tuesday. How many pages is that altogether? Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: Altogether means add the two amounts: 47 + 38 = ?. The answer is 85.

items.q: There are 92 people at the pool. 58 go home. How many are still at the pool? Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: Start with 92 and take away 58: 92 − 58 = ?. Put the bigger number first. The answer is 34.

items.q: Isla had some marbles. She gave away 40. Now she has 85 left. Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: We do not know the start. Take away 40 and 85 are left: ? − 40 = 85. The missing number is 125.

items.q: A footy team scored 64 points. The other team scored 19 fewer points. How many did the other team score? Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: 19 fewer means take away 19: 64 − 19 = ?. The answer is 45.

items.q: The hall needs 100 chairs for assembly. 57 chairs are set out. How many more are needed? Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: 57 and some more make 100: 57 + ? = 100. The missing number is 43.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, 160 students are at the pool. 70 of them are in the water. How many are not in the water?
items.e: Take away the 70 in the water. 16 tens − 7 tens = 9 tens, so 90 students.

items.q: Chloe scores 39 points in a game. Then she scores 26 more. How many points does she have now?
items.e: Add. 39 is 1 less than 40. 40 + 26 = 66, then take away 1: 65 points.

items.q: Year 3 Blue has 25 students. Year 3 Gold has 26 students. How many students are there in the two classes?
items.e: Use a near double. Double 25 is 50, and 1 more is 51 students.

items.q: The canteen had 250 icy poles. Some were sold. 160 are left. How many icy poles were sold?
Some students are on a bus. 30 more get on. Now there are 84 students. How many were on the bus at first?
items.e: ? + 30 = 84. Use the inverse: 84 − 30 = 54 students. Check: 54 + 30 = 84.

items.q: Leo has $1.20. He buys an apple at the canteen for 75c. How much money does he have left?
The sausage sizzle sells 148 sausages before lunch and 37 after lunch. How many sausages does it sell?
items.e: Add. 148 + 30 = 178, then 178 + 7: 178 + 2 = 180, and 5 more is 185 sausages.

items.q: A school has 412 students. 98 students go on an excursion. How many students stay at school?
items.e: 98 is 2 less than 100. 412 − 100 = 312. You took away 2 too many, so add them back: 314 students.

items.q: A library has 700 books. 260 books are borrowed. How many books are still on the shelves?
Mia has 64 footy cards. She gets 29 more. Then she gives 40 away. How many cards does she have now?
items.e: Step 1: 64 + 29 = 93 (add 30, take away 1). Step 2: 93 − 40 = 53 cards. (93 stops after step 1.)

items.q: Oliver buys a pie for $4.50 and a juice for $2.80. How much does he spend?
125 students are at the athletics carnival in the morning. More come after lunch. Now there are 200. How many students came after lunch?
